records.title: Untargeted metabolomics reveals immune-metabolic signatures in established cases of rheumatoid arthritis.
records.abstract_excerpt:
Introduction

Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a complex progressive autoimmune disorder wherein chronic inflammation is tightly coupled to metabolic reprogramming. The known diagnostic markers are not sensitive and specific enough to reflect disease activity. Finding a metabolomics-based biomarker specific for established cases of RA is important. This study aimed to investigate the metabolomic profiles of patients with established RA compared to those of controls.

**Revised Narrative**

The differential metabolite list is anchored by a strong enrichment signal in **Eicosanoid synthesis** (WikiPathways WP167; FDR = 0.0, fold-enrichment = 1,112), a term that captures the enzymatic oxidation of arachidonic acid into prostaglandins, leukotrienes, and hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acids. Five of the nine input metabolites are members of this pathway: arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 15-HETE, 5-HETE, and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2.

Arachidonic acid (KEGG C00219) acts as the upstream precursor hub. KEGG reaction-graph traversal confirms that it is linked to leukotriene A4 (C00909) via a two-step, bidirectional relationship through C05356, and to 15-HETE (C04742) via a forward path through C05966. Both arachidonic acid and leukotriene A4 are annotated in the SMPDB Arachidonic Acid Metabolism pathway (SMP00075), reinforcing their shared biological context. The simultaneous elevation of the downstream eicosanoid species (5-HETE, 15-HETE, leukotriene A4, and the cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2) against the backdrop of arachidonic acid availability is consistent with activated phospholipase A2 or cyclooxygenase/lipoxygenase activity — hallmark responses to inflammatory or oxidative-stress stimuli.

The remaining three metabolites — N-acetylgalactosamine (C01074), 2-ketobutyric acid (C00109), and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid (C00156) — were not enriched in the eicosanoid cluster; they likely reflect independent metabolic perturbations that remain to be characterized.

**Limitations:** Two input metabolites (2-ketobutyric acid, N-acetylgalactosamine) were not assigned to any enriched pathway at FDR < 0.05, so their biological relevance in this comparison rests on future validation. The prostaglandin 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-PGJ2 could not be placed on a KEGG reaction graph within six hops of arachidonic acid under default settings, limiting directional inference for that pair.
